evidence: Plin. Pan. 39: avus, avia, in a list of kin
Dig. 38.10.1: suprā avus, avia (Lewis & Short s.v. nepōs)
terms.comment: Latin has no single word for a grandparent of either sex: it names the pair. The masculine plural avī covers both, as parentēs and līberī do, but is as often grandfathers or forefathers.

evidence: Plin. Ep. 5.6.6: videās avōs proavōsque jam juvenum
Hor. C. 3.6.46: aetās parentum, pejor avīs
terms.comment: The plural of avus (see “grandfather”); in Horace the grandparents’ generation.

phrases.latin: Crās ad avum et aviam ībimus; jam nōs exspectant.
phrases.english: Tomorrow we’re going to Grandpa and Grandma’s; they’re expecting us already.
Give Grandpa and Grandma a kiss.

phrases.latin: Hinc senēs multī: videās avōs proavōsque jam juvenum, audiās fābulās veterēs sermōnēsque majōrum
phrases.english: So there are many old people: you can see the grandparents and great-grandparents of grown men, and hear old tales and the talk of the forefathers

sources: Lewis & Short: avus · Lewis & Short: avia
